status_summary: H.R. 2854, the Neighborhood Homes Investment Act, was introduced on 2025-04-10 and referred to the Ways and Means Committee; its identical Senate companion, S. 1686, was introduced on 2025-05-08 and referred to the Finance Committee. The BILLSTATUS records show no action on either bill since referral. The bill would create a tax credit for new construction and substantial rehabilitation of homes in eligible census tracts, including state-designated tracts in nonmetropolitan counties, plus a credit for rehabilitating owner-occupied homes; it is not specific to rural areas and uses the word rural only in its sense of Congress. No enacted rural renovation credit was found, and the CRS summary of the 2026 housing law lists no such credit.

timeline.event: H.R. 2854, the Neighborhood Homes Investment Act, was introduced and referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means; it provides a credit for rehabilitating homes in eligible tracts, including designated nonmetropolitan tracts.
S. 1686, the identical Senate Neighborhood Homes Investment Act (Sen. Young), was introduced and referred to the Senate Committee on Finance; it has had no later action recorded.

title: Create tax credits for renovation or repair of rural housing stock
uncertainties: The BILLSTATUS records for H.R. 2854 and S. 1686 on GovInfo were read in review; they show 70 and 9 cosponsors respectively and no action after referral, though BILLSTATUS may lag congress.gov, which could not be opened. The CRS report on Public Law 119-101 shows no rural housing tax credit; it increases income limits for USDA home repair loans, which is a loan program rather than a credit; that report and the housing provisions of Public Law 119-21 were not re-read in the latest review. Low-income housing tax credit changes in the 2025 reconciliation law are rental credits and were not assessed as a match. A rural-specific renovation credit bill was searched for once earlier and none was found; no new search was made in the latest review. The H.R. 2854 record also lists H.R. 6900 (American Affordability Act of 2025) and S. 4773 (DASH Act) as related bills; whether they carry the same credit and how far they advanced was not checked.
